findings.evidence: `class NormedSpace ... extends Module 𝕜 E` (mathlib/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Module/Basic.lean:40-41) already registers `NormedSpace.toModule` as an instance; `moduleOfNormedSpace` is literally `NormedSpace.toModule`, and being `private` does not stop the instance attribute from applying in every downstream file that imports this module, adding a second `Module ℝ E` search path for every normed space. The duplicated `universe`/`variable` lines at 349/351 vs 359/361 confirm the block is dead.

findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/RingTheory/IsTensorProduct.lean:367 `IsBaseChange.inductionOn (x : N) (motive : N → Prop) (zero) (tmul : ∀ m : M, motive (f m)) (smul) (add)`, with `h` an `include`d section variable so `hf.inductionOn` applies.

findings.issue: `span_range_eq_top_of_baseChange` is a 20-line detour (`Submodule.span_eq_top_of_span_eq_top`, two `map_span`s, `conv_rhs`, `le_antisymm`) that also needs a `change` at line 65 to strip the `⇑hf.equiv.toLinearMap` coercion.

findings.evidence: `Module.Flat.tensorProduct_mk_injective` is stated with `variable (R S M)` and instance binders (mathlib/Mathlib/RingTheory/Flat/Basic.lean:255-258); the nine-placeholder `@`-form in Lattice.lean:393 depends on that exact binder order. `DiscreteTopology.isDiscrete [DiscreteTopology s]` (mathlib/Mathlib/Topology/Constructions.lean:272) takes its instance by typeclass, so `haveI := hd; exact DiscreteTopology.isDiscrete` suffices.
findings.fix: Open each proof with `haveI := h.free` / `haveI := h.finite` (both classes are Props) and apply the lemmas by name; for the statements that need the instance in their type (`realBasis`, `realBasis_apply`), take `[Module.Free ℤ N] [Module.Finite ℤ N]` as instance binders on `IsIntegralLattice` instead of storing them as fields.
findings.issue: Instance plumbing is done with positional `@` applications and anonymous placeholders, which silently break or misresolve on any Mathlib binder reordering: `@Module.Flat.tensorProduct_mk_injective ℤ N _ _ _ ℝ _ _ _ (@Module.Flat.of_free ℤ N _ _ _ h.free)` (393-394), `@Module.Free.ChooseBasisIndex ℤ N _ _ _ h.free` (401, 408), `@Module.Free.chooseBasis ℤ N _ _ _ h.free` (410), `@DiscreteTopology.isDiscrete _ _ _ hd` (461), `@isDiscrete_range_of_instances N _ V₀ _ _ h.finite i h` (467).

findings.evidence: Lattice.lean:454-467: the helper's hypothesis `[Module.Finite ℤ N]` is instantiated at line 467 with `h.finite`, the field of the same `h` already passed as the last argument.
findings.fix: Delete the private helper and prove `IsIntegralLattice.isDiscrete_range` directly, starting with `haveI := h.finite`.
findings.issue: `isDiscrete_range_of_instances` exists only to introduce `[Module.Finite ℤ N]`, which is redundant with `h : IsIntegralLattice i` (it carries `h.finite`); `isDiscrete_range` then re-supplies it via `@...h.finite`.

findings.evidence: Lattice.lean:421-425: the local instance is introduced immediately before `hrange'`, whose statement `Submodule.span ℤ (Set.range (realBasis i h))` elaborates against the ambient instance.
findings.fix: Drop the `let` if it is redundant; if it is load-bearing, state which instance it overrides and why, or restructure so the span is taken with the instance already present in the statement.
findings.issue: `let _ : Module ℤ (ℝ ⊗[ℤ] N) := TensorProduct.instModule` installs a local ℤ-action instance that shadows the ambient one for the rest of the proof; the comment ("Align the tensor product's scalar action...") does not say which competing instance it displaces or why the goal's instance is wrong. Mathlib's ℤ-module instances are only propositionally unique (`Subsingleton (Module ℤ M)`), so this makes the proof depend on which of two instances elaboration happens to pick.

summary: The new proofs carry substantial instance-plumbing scaffolding (positional `@` applications, a redundant private `Module ℝ` instance, a shadowing local `Module ℤ` instance, a `local instance` priority hack that expires before the code it was meant to serve) and close goals through undocumented coercion defeq (`change`, `congr 1`). The 20-line `span_range_eq_top_of_baseChange` is also a detour around Mathlib's `IsBaseChange.inductionOn`.
